title_en: OI24: Why Power Trading Is 10 Times Crazier Than Crypto ft. Cory Paddock
title_zh: OI24：电力交易为何比加密货币疯狂十倍（ft. GBE 联合创始人 Cory Paddock）
subtitle_zh: GBE 联合创始人 Cory Paddock 讲述电力市场的极端波动、日内交易逻辑与自营交易人才培养之道
summary_zh: 本期 Top Traders Unplugged 的 Open Interest 系列由 Moritz Seibert 对话 GBE Energy 联合创始人 Cory Paddock——这是该系列首次请到一家自营交易公司（prop trading firm）而非管理外部资金的对冲基金。GBE（寓意 God Bless Everyone）成立于 2013 年，总部位于加拿大 Calgary 与 White Rock，团队由交易员、气象学家、量化开发人员与市场分析师组成，专注交易美国电力市场、尤其是覆盖 13 个州的 PJM。节目以“电力交易比加密货币疯狂十倍”点出这一市场的极端波动：电力正好处在物理学、天气、经济学与市场设计的交汇点上，其起源可追溯到上世纪八九十年代人们发现优化电力系统经济性的根本洞见。Paddock 讲解了北美电网按西部互联、东部互联等相对独立运行、各区资源禀赋（resource endowment）差异巨大，以及系统运营商在可靠性与最低发电成本之间始终向可靠性倾斜的实时平衡；GBE 的盈利核心在于对负荷与发电的精准理解——下一兆瓦来自哪里。他与搭档 Jerry Zhang 的平均持仓约 10 至 12 小时，本质是日内生意，最关键的技艺在于识别出价格爆发的日子并敢于重仓。Paddock 如今更多转向招募与培养年轻交易员，强调概率化思维（probabilistic thinking）、情绪沉稳、韧性与不被结果蒙蔽的学习能力等教不会的特质，并结合其运动员背景与交易心理展开。是一堂难得的小众市场机制与自营交易人才培养课。

turns.zh: 不仅是经济层面，还有维持电网可靠性。是的，而电网可靠性意味着，你知道，你必须几乎不间断地让电网和负荷保持平衡，否则瞬间就会停电，而且是全天候 24/7/365 都要如此。

turns.zh: 是啊，这是个好问题。我们大部分交易都是在 ICE 交易所上做的，也就是洲际交易所（Intercontinental Exchange），很多大宗商品都在那儿交易。但我们主要交易一个叫做 PJM West Hub 的产品，这是个很奇怪的产品，因为它是 PJM 系统内一个个独立交易节点（trading node）汇成的一个枢纽（hub）。其中一堆节点位于 Western Pennsylvania，另一堆节点位于 Washington D.C. 及其周边，所以在地理上有点分散。但那份

turns.zh: 运作方式和原油或天然气类似，也就是有按整年（calendar years）延展的合约，然后逐渐过渡到近月（prompt months）或者往后几个月的合约。但它和北美天然气产品不同的地方在于，你实际上会开始得到多得多的颗粒度（granularity），细到单个星期、剩余周（balance of weeks）、次日（next day），甚至当天或者说当日剩余（balance of day，也就是 BAL PJM），这是我们多年来花了很多时间、并且继续花

turns.en: lot of time on. turns.zh: 大量时间的产品。这个产品本身，是每天所有那些节点在第 8 小时到第 23 小时（hour ending 8 到 hour ending 23）之间 5 分钟价格的加权平均，覆盖每一个高负荷日（heavy load day），也就是周内的工作日，所以是每一天。这份合约的独特之处还在于，随着你在一天的进程中推进，一堆单独的 5 分钟价格、以及最终的每小时价格会变得已知，但当天剩下的时间里仍然有一大堆未知数，日内仍然会有大量波动性

turns.en: can happen. turns.zh: 会发生。所以尽管这些年信息已经改进了很多，尤其是在天气预报方面，你会以为当我们距离明天只有 24 小时的时候，我们已经知道电网会怎么运行了。但结果其实是——不，我们并不真正知道那天电力实际上会怎么流动。

turns.en: Typically it's, I mean, this is going to sound a little bit pithy, but we try to understand what demand is going to look like and we try to understand what supply is going to look like and if there's a mismatch. So I mean, it's a little bit more complicated than that. But on the load side there's a lot of interesting variables. So it's a lot more tricky than just saying, oh, we think demand is going to be high or low. There's differences in demand between different sub regions and that can impact power, impact
turns.zh: 通常是这样，我是说，这听起来会有点老套，但我们努力去理解需求会长什么样，努力去理解供给会长什么样，以及两者之间是否存在错配。所以我是说，它比这要更复杂一些。在负荷（load）这一侧有很多有意思的变量。所以它比单纯地说“哦，我们觉得需求会高或低”要棘手得多。不同子区域之间的需求是有差异的，而这会影响电力、影响

turns.en: power flow. So we pay a lot of attention to that. There's various inflection points for load depending on the weather. So there's actually typically PGM and still is remains a summer peaking system, meaning demand is highest during the summer when kind of AC is running highest. But there's actually some sub zones within PGM that are transitioning more to winter peaking, whereby winter heating demand is actually exceeding summer AC demand. So that's one thing that's gradually shifting over time. And so throughout
turns.zh: 电力潮流（power flow）。所以我们对此非常关注。负荷会根据天气有各种各样的拐点（inflection point）。所以实际上，PJM 通常是、而且现在仍然是一个夏季尖峰（summer peaking）系统，意思是需求在夏天最高，也就是空调开得最猛的时候。但 PJM 内部实际上有一些子区域正在更多地转向冬季尖峰（winter peaking），也就是冬季取暖需求实际上超过了夏季空调需求。所以这是随时间逐渐变化的一个点。而在一整天的

turns.en: the day, each of these days have different load shapes and those shapes differ by season, by time of day, by sun angle. And so we try to understand load
turns.zh: 过程中，每一天都有不同的负荷形状（load shape），而这些形状会因季节、因一天中的时段、因太阳角度而不同。所以要真正理解——基本上就是理解整个市场、或者说市场整体上对负荷究竟是多少有没有一个好的判断——这里面涉及相当多的变量。所以我们会努力去理解负荷，

turns.en: really, really well. First and foremost, I would say yeah, a lot of our trades are kind of downstream of that. turns.en: One of the reasons I'm addicted to systems trading is that I don't need to have that conversation with myself as to who's right or not or whether I'm smarter than anybody else. The system tells us to get out and we follow the system. End of story.
turns.zh: 我之所以迷上系统化交易（systems trading），原因之一就是我不需要跟自己进行那种对话，去争谁对谁错、或者我是不是比别的任何人都聪明。系统叫我们退出，我们就跟着系统走。就这样，没什么好说的。

turns.en: Yeah, that makes it easier on that, on that front quite a bit. Yep.
turns.zh: 是啊，在那一方面，这让它轻松了不少。没错。

turns.en: You mentioned that you were too stubborn to get out of the trade psychology of trading and I want to move into the recruiting part. My understanding, Corey, is that if I remember that correctly from our pre call, you're not currently trading anymore. You're much more focused on running the business, recruiting people and teaching them how to trade. So you freed yourself from looking at the markets, running a book and positions and risk 247 or at least for a big, big part of the day and you have no other people
turns.zh: 你提到你当时太固执，没能及时退出那笔交易——交易心理。我想转到招募这部分。我的理解是，Cory，如果我没记错我们节目前的通话内容的话，你现在已经不再做交易了。你更多地专注于经营公司、招募人、教他们怎么交易。所以你把自己从盯市场、运营账簿、仓位和风险这种全天候、或者至少一天里很大一部分时间里解放了出来，而且你现在让其他人来

turns.en: to it. Tell us a bit about how that works at GBE and why you've changed that recruiting process so that you're now focusing on getting motivated and hungry young, aspiring traders into the firm, as opposed to the veterans and experienced traders that obviously demand a bigger paycheck and have different ambitions.
turns.zh: 接手这件事。给我们讲讲这在 GBE 是怎么运作的，以及你们为什么改变了那个招募流程，好让你们现在专注于把有动力、有闯劲、有抱负的年轻交易员招进公司，而不是那些显然要求更高薪水、也有不同抱负的老将和有经验的交易员。

turns.en: So how does it work? That's a good question. When I look back on the past couple of years
turns.zh: 那这是怎么运作的？这是个好问题。当我回顾过去这几年

turns.en: and this whole process, it's been hugely gratifying, but at the same time infuriating at times because I've been coincidentally seeing the market really, really well and trying to teach young people what I'm seeing and when they should and shouldn't be executing. So we came to this insight just over three years ago
turns.zh: 以及这整个过程，它极其令人欣慰，但同时又时不时令人抓狂，因为我恰好把市场看得非常、非常清楚，还要努力去教年轻人我看到的东西、以及他们什么时候该执行、什么时候不该执行。所以我们是刚刚三年多以前得到这个洞见的，

turns.en: and we were originally actually inspired by our partner firm in the U.S. greenwich Commodities, which trades in the same markets, but trades financial transmission rights. That would be an entire other podcast to describe that craziness.
turns.zh: 而且我们最初其实是受到我们在美国的合作公司 Greenwich Commodities 的启发，它在同样的市场里交易，但交易的是金融输电权（financial transmission rights，FTR）。要描述那种疯狂，够做整整另一期播客了。

turns.en: But they had been quite successful in, in recruiting interns
turns.zh: 但他们在招募实习生方面一直相当成功，

turns.en: and teaching them, developing them, progressing them through internship into analysts and then associate traders and then full time traders after that. So we got inspired that it could be done in the first place. The other thing that happened is, I mean, we, Jerry and myself, we looked at each other and a little bit too late, but not too, too late, and discovered, you know, we're old.
turns.zh: 教他们、培养他们，让他们从实习生一路晋升到分析师，然后到助理交易员（associate traders），再到全职交易员。所以我们受到的启发是：这件事首先是可以做成的。发生的另一件事是，我是说，我和 Jerry，我们俩互相看了看——有点太晚了，但还不算太太晚——然后发现，你知道，我们老了。

turns.en: You know, I'm, I'm 46 at this point, but for, for a trader, that's pretty old. And we hadn't done a great job of, of developing our own tacit knowledge in these markets into another generation of traders. And so like you mentioned in the opening, traditionally we'd been working with more senior traders and then offering them a platform to apply their craft, and not only apply their craft, but have a, you know, 100% certainty over their compensation,
turns.zh: 你知道，我现在 46 岁，但对一个交易员来说，这已经算相当老了。而且我们在把自己在这些市场里的隐性知识（tacit knowledge）传承给下一代交易员这件事上，做得并不好。所以就像你开场时提到的，传统上我们一直和更资深的交易员合作，然后给他们提供一个平台去施展他们的手艺，不仅是施展手艺，还能对自己的薪酬有 100% 的确定性，

turns.en: which is a big question mark still in a lot of the bigger firms where, you know, bonuses are still very discretionary. And as a trader, one of your biggest stresses is after you wheel through all the pain of having a great year in the first place, am I actually going to get paid on this thing? So that's, that's one piece of the equation we wanted to just eliminate and still eliminate as a part of our strategy and culture, really. So anyway, we decided to really get serious about trying to pass along our knowledge
turns.zh: 而在很多更大的公司里，这仍然是个大问号，你知道，奖金仍然非常靠自由裁量（discretionary）。而作为一名交易员，你最大的压力之一就是：在你熬过了做出一个漂亮年份的所有痛苦之后，我到底能不能真的拿到这笔钱？所以这是我们想要直接消除的一块，而且至今仍要把它消除掉，作为我们战略和文化的一部分。总之，我们决定真正认真地着手去传承我们的知识

turns.en: and our way of trading. I guess the other insight that we had
turns.zh: 以及我们的交易方式。我想我们拥有的另一个洞见是，

turns.en: was we weren't really that confident that other more senior firms or established firms were recruiting well in the first place. And so if we continued on with our previous strategy, it would be depending on all those other firms recruiting people into the industry in the first place. So we felt like we could tell the story of power trading and why it's so compelling. And then also the story of YGPE is compelling and a great place to learn.
turns.zh: 我们其实并不那么有信心，觉得其它那些更资深的公司或成熟公司一开始就把招募做得很好。所以如果我们继续沿用之前的策略，那就要依赖于所有那些其它公司先把人招进这个行业。于是我们觉得，我们能够讲好电力交易的故事、讲清楚它为什么这么有吸引力，也能讲好 GBE 为什么有吸引力、为什么是个学习的好地方这样的故事。

turns.en: And I think that thesis has been validated now that we're kind of three years into this. So those are kind of the fundamental insights. The other thing that was happening that we felt would be kind of in our way or would help support the view was particularly right at that time. We felt like we were getting into this inflection point that we would have gone through when we were coming up in that we used to demonstrate our mastery of Excel and our seniors used to think that we were wizards. And now we're in a period
turns.zh: 而且我觉得，如今我们做这件事差不多三年了，这个论点已经得到了验证。所以这些大致就是那些根本性的洞见。当时正在发生的另一件事，我们觉得它要么会挡我们的路、要么会帮助支撑这个观点，尤其是在那个时候——我们觉得我们正在进入这样一个拐点，就像我们自己成长起来时经历过的那样：那时我们靠展示自己精通 Excel，让前辈们觉得我们是巫师。而现在我们正处在一个时期，

turns.en: where these young people under 25 and what they can do with LLMs is extraordinary. Now, do they still need an extraordinary or a high amount of context that sits within the tacit knowledge of firms? Absolutely right. It's not like you can just give a young person a bunch of capital and say, go make money in power markets.
turns.zh: 这些 25 岁以下的年轻人，他们用大语言模型（LLM）能做到的事情非同寻常。那么，他们是否仍然需要大量存在于公司隐性知识之中的背景（context）？绝对需要。这不是说你可以直接给一个年轻人一堆资本，然后说：去电力市场里赚钱吧。

turns.en: No, you still need to know and bully the LLMs into the right answer.
turns.zh: 不行，你仍然需要懂行，并且把 LLM“逼”出正确的答案来。

turns.en: But the speed at which models and tools can be turned around has been continuously surprising to me. And I would say just the seriousness in which this cohort of young people takes their craft and takes the work. We've been very impressed by.
turns.zh: 但模型和工具能够被迭代出来的速度，一直让我感到惊讶。而且我会说，这一批年轻人对待自己手艺、对待工作的那份认真，让我们印象深刻。

turns.en: The. Maybe that's the wrong word, average recruiter, average analyst that you're who are getting on board. Do they need to have a fascination for the power markets or are you more looking like, yeah, there's a person that just wants to be a trader, whether that equities or bonds or currencies, trading. Like somebody that kind of has an interest in markets and you take it from there.
turns.zh: 那个……也许我用错词了。你们招进来的那些普通的应聘者、普通的分析师，他们需要对电力市场有一种着迷吗？还是说你们更多是在找那种——是啊，有个人就是想当交易员，无论是股票、债券还是外汇交易。就是那种对市场有点兴趣的人，然后你们从这里开始带。

turns.en: Maybe they should know what a bit of an offer is. And the rest you're trying to teach them or you're looking for a little bit more in these people.
turns.zh: 也许他们应该稍微懂一点什么是“报价（offer）”。剩下的你们去教他们，或者说你们在这些人身上要找的东西还要更多一点。

turns.en: We are looking for individuals that have a demonstrated passion for trading. They can feel it in their soul that they want to trade
turns.zh: 我们要找的是那些已经展现出对交易的热情的个体。他们能在灵魂深处感受到自己想要交易，

turns.en: and they just don't know power exists. And really they're agnostic into how they want to apply their craft. They just know they want to trade. And oftentimes that gets expressed in trading their own account, building their own models, being at clubs, in school,
turns.zh: 只是他们此前不知道电力这个东西存在。而且实际上，对于自己想怎么施展这门手艺，他们是无所谓、不设限的（agnostic）。他们只是知道自己想交易。而这种欲望常常表现为：交易自己的账户、搭建自己的模型、参加学校里的社团、

turns.en: sports gambling, online poker, online gambling. So there's just an inherent drive and will to make money and to put on risk. And from there that's, in my view, the unteachable part is whether somebody wants it badly enough. And that's very much where. That's my own bias. That's where I kind of. That's my background. And then for somebody that has that kind of will, they'll go and learn the fundamentals, provided that they've got enough context and where to go and where and how they can learn that stuff, they'll
turns.zh: 体育博彩、在线扑克、在线赌博。所以就有一种与生俱来的驱动力和意愿，去赚钱、去承担风险。而从那里开始，在我看来，那部分教不会的东西就是：一个人是否足够渴望它。而这很大程度上正是——这是我自己的偏好。这正是我某种程度上——这是我的背景所在。然后对于一个有那种意愿的人来说，他们会去学基本面，前提是他们有足够的背景、知道去哪儿学、以及怎么学那些东西，他们就会

turns.en: go and do the work. And we've seen this time and time again with our most talented young people.
turns.zh: 去下这个功夫。而在我们最有才华的那些年轻人身上，我们一次又一次地看到了这一点。

turns.en: How long does that process take? So you have that person that has demonstrated a will to trade. That's what they want to do, that's their passion. But then they arrive at tbe. Maybe they know nothing or close to nothing about the power markets. What, what's the time period like? I mean, is this kind of like a three year or five year, one year educational process and then they go live or how long does it take?
turns.zh: 这个过程要花多长时间？所以你有了那个已经展现出交易意愿的人。那是他们想做的事，那是他们的热情所在。但他们来到 GBE 时，也许对电力市场一无所知，或者几乎一无所知。那么这个时间段大概是什么样？我是说，这是一个三年、五年，还是一年的培养过程，然后他们才真正上线交易，还是说这需要多久？

turns.en: It's a lot shorter than I would have thought. Okay. I think when we first started off, our mental model was that it probably would take a young intern and analyst about a year.
turns.zh: 它比我原本以为的要短得多。好。我想我们刚开始的时候，我们的思维模型是，一个年轻的实习生和分析师大概需要一年时间。

turns.en: Like an entire full cycle to go through and probably longer, actually. Probably like 16 to 18 months. So not like see an entire season, see an entire year. So see the winter season, the shoulder season, see the summer season of just analysis before they would be kind of even ready to make calls and be useful to the firm. But instead, what we've seen is in our most recent cases, that has been condensed down to six to eight months.
turns.zh: 也就是走完一整个完整的周期，实际上可能还要更长。大概像 16 到 18 个月。所以不是看一整个季节、看一整个年份。而是要看过冬季、过渡季（shoulder season）、夏季，只做分析，然后他们才差不多准备好去做出判断、对公司有用。但相反，我们在最近的这些案例里看到的是，这已经被压缩到了六到八个月。

turns.en: Wow. I'd say that's pretty fast. I think so too. But at the same time, we feel like we've seen enough in the work and the understanding of what's going on
turns.zh: 哇。我会说那是相当快了。我也这么觉得。但与此同时，我们觉得，在他们的工作、以及他们对正在发生什么的理解上，我们已经看到了足够多的东西，

turns.en: for these individuals to deploy capital. Yeah, we've been quite impressed and yeah, we're going to keep going.
turns.zh: 足以让这些人去部署资本了。是啊，我们印象相当深刻，而且是的，我们会继续这么做下去。

turns.en: So to the young and aspiring traders out there listening to us, go to the GBA website, give Corey a call. I assume this recruiting process is still ongoing. If you find the right.
turns.zh: 所以，对正在听我们节目、那些年轻而有抱负的交易员们，去 GBE 的网站，给 Cory 打个电话。我猜这个招募过程还在继续。如果你们找到了对的人的话。

turns.en: It's still ongoing. It's still ongoing. I say this pretty often depending on in a number of different circumstances, but Jerry and I are quite rational, greedy business people. And when something's working, we're going to keep doing it. And it's working, so we're going to keep doing it.
turns.zh: 它还在继续。还在继续。这句话我在很多不同的场合都挺常说的：我和 Jerry 是相当理性、贪婪的生意人。当某件事奏效的时候，我们就会一直做下去。而它现在奏效，所以我们会一直做下去。

turns.en: Good. As we're closing this down, Corey, what's your outlook for the power markets? I mean, yeah, I'm not sure if it makes sense to talk about prices, but more like, I mean, I guess these markets will grow. We're going to electrify our societies. We're going to be More dependent on power for AI, for, you know, EVs, for the,
turns.zh: 很好。在我们收尾的时候，Cory，你对电力市场的展望是什么？我是说，是啊，我不确定谈论价格有没有意义，但更多的是——我是说，我想这些市场会增长。我们要让我们的社会电气化。我们要在 AI、电动车（EV）、

turns.en: for the ecological transition that we're all working on. I mean, do you foresee that these markets will become larger, more liquid, more volume, more participants, more competitive, which wouldn't necessarily be a good thing for the alpha generation piece of your business? Or would you rather think, no, that's kind of like it's still too much of a niche opaque stuff, too complex and a lot of people will therefore stay out of it?
turns.zh: 以及我们大家正在努力的生态转型上，更多地依赖电力。我是说，你预见到这些市场会变得更大、流动性更强、成交量更多、参与者更多、竞争更激烈吗？——而这对你生意里产生 alpha 的那部分未必是件好事。还是说你更愿意认为，不，这东西还是太小众、太不透明、太复杂，因此很多人会敬而远之、待在外面？

turns.en: I think both of those scenarios are possible. Okay,. Going back to, even back 10 years ago, I would have thought it would have been inevitable over time that the market would have grown and we would have seen more and more participants enter into the arena. And we haven't necessarily seen that it's been a little bit more of a slower growth. But we can have a conversation around how bullish we want to be about AI, but the direction is still up and to the right. It's just a matter of how steep the
turns.zh: 我觉得这两种情形都有可能。好。即便回到 10 年前，我原本会以为，随着时间推移，市场增长、我们会看到越来越多的参与者进入这个竞技场，这是不可避免的。但我们并不一定看到了这一点，它更多是一种偏慢的增长。不过，关于我们对 AI 想有多看多，我们可以好好聊聊，但方向仍然是向右上方的。这只是这条曲线有多陡峭

turns.en: curve is. So the data center build out is still going to happen.
turns.zh: 的问题。所以数据中心的建设仍然会发生。

turns.en: Electrification of vehicles is still going to happen. Electrification of heat and buildings and further additions of air conditioning, that's still going to happen. It's just a matter of again, what are the time periods and the speed in which it's going to actually happen. But I think largely speaking, there's not a better commodity to be in. I mean, I'm pretty biased for the next 10 years. And there'll be cycles for sure. There'll be some stint of oversupply
turns.zh: 车辆的电气化仍然会发生。供热和建筑的电气化、以及空调的进一步增加，那仍然会发生。这同样只是时间段和它实际发生的速度的问题。但我觉得大体上说，没有比这更好的大宗商品可以置身其中了。我是说，未来 10 年我相当有偏好（biased）。而且肯定会有周期。会有一段时间的供给过剩，

turns.en: and then probably some stint of undersupply again in the same way that commodities have always been. But as you said, it's pretty impossible to imagine any kind of future human civilization with less electricity.
turns.zh: 然后很可能又会有一段时间的供给不足，就像大宗商品一直以来那样。但正如你说的，几乎无法想象任何一种用电更少的未来人类文明。

turns.en: I mean, it goes through these cycles here in Europe too. Sometimes you have a bank offering a product for retail investors to invest. And I think if this I might be completely wrong, but it may have been Barclays or Citibank and maybe that's 20 years ago they came up with an index kind of like or an ETN tracking US power markets.
turns.zh: 我是说，在欧洲这边也会经历这些周期。有时候你会有一家银行面向散户投资者提供一个投资产品。而且我想，这一点我可能完全记错了，但那可能是 Barclays 或者 Citibank，大概是 20 年前，他们推出了一个类似指数、或者追踪美国电力市场的 ETN。

turns.en: And I think more recently an ETF came out doing the same thing. I'm not entirely sure. So it kind of goes to show, yeah, there's like if things in the news, AI, power, demand, lo and behold, sooner than later, there's going to be a product, most likely an ETF form coming to the market so that everybody can participate in it. But then it's more like tracking along power exposure, which
turns.zh: 而且我想最近又有一只 ETF 出来做同样的事情。我不完全确定。所以这多少说明了，是啊，如果某样东西上了新闻——AI、电力、需求——瞧吧，迟早会有一个产品、很可能是 ETF 的形式，来到市场上，让每个人都能参与其中。但那样它更多是追踪一篮子电力敞口，而这

turns.en: may not necessarily be the best thing to always be long, that stuff. Given that you've explained to us that there is a risk premium in there and most of the time you like to be short.
turns.zh: 未必是最好的东西去一直做多。既然你已经向我们解释了，那里面存在一个风险溢价（risk premium），而且大部分时间你都喜欢做空。

turns.en: Unless you get into this new paradigm shift, which I feel like we might be halfway into. I guess the argument against a huge proliferation or expansion of the industry writ large would be
turns.zh: 除非你进入这个新的范式转变，而我觉得我们可能已经走到一半了。我想，反对整个行业大规模扩散或扩张的那个论点是，

turns.en: there hasn't been a market design that has really solved the physics and economics problem. So if that's the case, then you can imagine a world where pockets of power markets exist kind of throughout the world, and each of those pockets have their own idiosyncrasies, different rules, different politics, and then they stay reasonably insular and very niche. And that's another scenario that's entirely possible. But in either direction, I'm comfortable. I think
turns.zh: 至今还没有一种市场设计真正解决了物理学和经济学的问题。所以如果是这样的话，你就能想象这样一个世界：世界各地零散地存在一些电力市场的小块（pockets），而每一块都有它们自己的特质、不同的规则、不同的政治，然后它们保持相对封闭、非常小众。那是另一种完全可能的情形。但无论朝哪个方向，我都很坦然。我想

turns.en: we'll be fine regardless. Great, Corey. I think this is a great time to bring the conversation to a close. It's about an hour and I hope that we have not overwhelmed the audience.
